% Invented deck exercising the slide chrome end to end: the footer (a
% declared section title left, the theme's frame number right, in the muted
% key at the small step), a beamer-style framefooter wrapper whose \setbeamertemplate
% reaches the same footer through \framefoot, and the return to the default
% when the wrapper ends. Nothing here derives from any private document.
\documentclass[aspectratio=169]{beamer}

\usetheme{moloch}
% The section title in the left slot is this deck's own declaration: the
% bundle's footline (the dtx) leaves that slot to \framefoot.
\chrome{ footer = { left = \sectiontitle } }

\fonts{
  dir = "fonts",
  body = "Open Sans",
}

\newenvironment{framefooter}[1]{\setbeamertemplate{frame footer}{#1}}{\setbeamertemplate{frame footer}{}}

\title{Slide Chrome}
\author{Pat Placeholder}

\begin{document}

\maketitle

\section{Footers}

\begin{frame}{Default}
  The footer names the section and the frame.
\end{frame}

\begin{framefooter}{source: example.org/data --- invented}
\begin{frame}{Attributed}
  This frame carries its own footer note beside the frame number.
\end{frame}
\end{framefooter}

\begin{frame}{Back to default}
  The wrapper ended, so the section title returns.
\end{frame}

\end{document}
